# Purpose

JABBA and SPiCT share a biomass-production model: surplus production, catch,
and an abundance index. FLICC, kept as a yield-per-recruit calculation, does
not. Its inputs are an `FLStock` (life history, maturity, selectivity) and an
F grid. Putting FLICC on the Pella–Tomlinson object used for JABBA and SPiCT
mixes two different models.

The shared piece is the prior thread in
`vignettes/prior-thread-jabba-spict-flicc.Rmd`: one canonical table, then a
separate adapter for each model. `asFliccPriors()` maps that table onto FLICC
scalars. `asFliccPriorsYpr()` does not use it. It builds the per-recruit curve
from the stock.

# Objects

1. `FLPar` holds the life-history parameters (growth, mortality, maturity).
2. An `FLStock` carries those schedules at age, plus the selectivity in
   `harvest`.
3. `asFliccPriorsYpr()` sweeps F and returns yield per recruit and spawning
   potential per recruit.

# The YPR adapter

```{r ypr, eval=FALSE}
library(FLCore)
library(FLRebuild)

data(ple4)
ypr <- asFliccPriorsYpr(ple4, fRange = c(0, 2), nF = 101, priorCv = 0.30)

ypr$reference
head(ypr$curve)
ypr$canonical
```

`reference` contains `fMsyProxy`, `yprMsyProxy`, `spr0`, `sprAtFmsy` and
`sprRatioAtFmsy`. `curve` is the F grid with `ypr` and `spr`. `canonical` is
the same scalars in the prior-thread shape, with standard deviations from
`priorCv`, so a YPR run can be set beside a production run without pretending
they share a dynamic model.

`selectivity` overrides the harvest-at-age pattern. Leave it `NULL` to
normalise the stock's own harvest.

# What is not shared

Do not pass a JABBA or SPiCT production fit into `asFliccPriorsYpr()`.
Reference points from the two tracks can still be tabulated together after
both exist. The comparison is then explicit: per-recruit equilibrium against
biomass-dynamic equilibrium, not two views of one fitted object.
